name: isOfFinAddOrder_of_finite
script:
have h₁ : ∃ (G : Type u_1) [inst : AddLeftCancelMonoid G] [Finite G], ¬ (∀ (x : G), IsOfFinAddOrder x) := by
  classical
  -- Consider the trivial group {0} with one element.
  use ℤMod 1
  infer_instance
  <;>
  (try decide) <;>
  (try {
    intro h
    have h₂ := h (⟨0, by decide⟩ : ℤMod 1)
    -- The element ⟨0, _⟩ is the only element in ℤMod 1.
    -- We need to show that it does not have finite additive order.
    simp [IsOfFinAddOrder] at h₂
    <;>
    aesop
  }) <;>
  (try {
    -- The trivial group {0} has one element, so the statement is vacuously true.
    aesop
  })
-- Use the existence of a counterexample to prove the main theorem.
obtain ⟨G, _, _, h₂⟩ := h₁
intro h₃
have h₄ : ∀ (x : G), IsOfFinAddOrder x := by
  intro x
  exact h₃ x
-- This leads to a contradiction because h₂ states that not all elements in G are of finite additive order.
exact h₂ h₄
